tip.1: Hold Tab to see the whole interface: the bars, the clock, the map and the money.
tip.2: Tap F to go back to the tool you had before; hold it for the tool wheel.
tip.3: Click on the map to mark a route; right click removes it.
tip.4: Tap W, then press and hold it to jog; two taps and a hold to sprint.
tip.5: A tap of Shift crouches; hold it to sit on the ground.
tip.6: Aim at a river, a lake or a well and press E to drink.
tip.7: Sea water is too salty to drink.
tip.8: Muddy or dirty? Press X at the water's edge to scrub yourself.
tip.9: Sleep in a bed to fill your energy.
tip.10: Press Y to greet whoever you aim at: the neighbors remember it.
tip.11: Chat with the neighbours: that is how you learn what they like and wish for.
tip.12: Press N to whistle for your horse; the closer the bond, the farther it hears you.
tip.13: Brushing your horse and giving it carrots makes the bond grow.
tip.14: A winded horse only trots: let it get its breath back.
tip.15: The saddlebags carry 12 stacks and their weight isn't on you.
tip.16: A felled tree leaves a log: carry it on your shoulder with E.
tip.17: The wheelbarrow moves what you can't carry.
tip.18: Building and crafting also use what is in the chests nearby.
tip.19: Large things are built with B and need their station nearby.
tip.20: Nilo, Dani and Anselmo sell the plans of the furniture.
tip.21: With B, Move lets you change a piece of furniture's place for free.
tip.22: Hold R to turn what you are about to place little by little.
tip.23: Water before the soil dries out: nothing grows without it.
tip.24: Crops grow by the weather, not the calendar: frost kills the tender ones.
tip.25: Grass grows back a few days after it is cut or grazed.
tip.26: Each fish has its season, its hours and its water.
tip.27: A hunted animal leaves a carcass: butcher it with X before it spoils.
tip.28: Arrows that miss can be picked up again.
tip.29: Cold? Wear wool or leather, or stay by a fire.
tip.30: Wet clothes chill you: dry off by the fire or under a roof.
tip.31: Clothes wear out with work: mend them at the loom or at Marta's.
tip.32: Hair and beard grow with the days: the barber's chair fixes that.
tip.33: While swimming, hold Shift to dive and Space to come up.
tip.34: Watch the air bar under water.
tip.35: The deeper the cave, the better the ore.
tip.36: Carry torches into the caves: it is pitch dark down there.
tip.37: The shovel digs and drops earth: next to water, the holes fill up.
tip.38: A well gives water all year round.
tip.39: The world goes on for everybody while you are in the menu.
tip.40: The game saves by itself; you can quit whenever you like.
gui.controls.title: Controls
controls.walk: Walk (up is where the camera is looking)
controls.run: Jog: tap W, then press it again and hold it (it uses no energy). Sprint: tap W twice and hold it on the third press (it drains the energy bar; out of breath, you drop to a jog). Let go of W and you stop; the next press walks again. Riding, one press walks, the second canters (it trots on the way up) and the third gallops; swimming, a steady crawl and a fast swim
controls.crouch: Posture. A tap: crouch, or stand up if you're crouching. Hold it: sit on the ground; sitting, hold it again to lie face up (a tap brings you up one step: lying, you sit up; sitting, you crouch). Walking gets you up. While crouching you move slowly, make less noise and wild animals see you from closer, and what you place doesn't connect to its neighbors. While swimming, Shift dives: hold it to go down, and Space to come up
controls.use: Use what you're holding: chop, mine, water, sow, fish, attack, eat, place… Hold to keep going.
controls.jump: Jump (in a dialogue: continue). While swimming, hold it to come up; at the surface next to the shore, climb out
controls.interact: Interact with what you point at with the mouse (2 tiles away at most; pointing at nothing, with the nearest thing): talk, doors, chests, stations, sleep, harvest, animals. What each key does shows at the thing; a key with a ring has to be held
controls.drink: Thirsty, aim at a river, a lake or a well to drink (one press drinks until you're full; moving stops it). Sea water is too salty. With a canteen or a jug in hand: click for a sip, E or click on fresh water to fill it
controls.wash: Muddy, dirty or bloody: aim at a river, a lake or the sea while wading or from the bank to scrub yourself (about 8 s; moving stops it). E on a bathtub takes a bath, and E on a basin washes your face and hands. Soap in your bag washes you fully clean
controls.body: Under the bars, only when it matters: Cold, Freezing, Hot, Soaked or Filthy. Hold Tab to see how warm you feel
controls.clothes: Clothes wear out with tool work, sprinting through the woods, lying on the ground, swimming dressed and hits; the bar in their slot shows what is left, and torn clothes keep you less warm. Mend them at the loom (C: one cloth, wool or leather) or for coins with Marta, at the tavern in the evening, who also sells warm clothes by season. The neighbours notice how you look and remember what you do
controls.bars: Top left: health, hunger, thirst and energy (and air under water). Food fills hunger, drink fills thirst and sleeping in a bed fills energy; health comes back by itself when you're fed and watered. Hover them (or hold Tab) to see their %
controls.rotate: Rotate what you're about to place (aim with the mouse: up to 4 tiles). Held, it keeps turning; tapped, in 15° steps, snapping to the tiles
controls.camera_turn: Turn the camera around you (hold: smooth turn)
controls.camera_tilt: Raise the camera until you almost see from above, or lower it to ground level
controls.zoom: Zoom the camera in and out
controls.view: First or third person (in first person, <kbd>↑</kbd> <kbd>↓</kbd> look up and down)
controls.wheel: Tool wheel: hold it, move the mouse and let go to equip (playing alone, the game goes in slow motion meanwhile). A tap goes back to what you held before
controls.windows: Inventory (what you carry and your clothes), crafting and building
controls.journal_map: Journal and map (two tabs of the pause; the same key again closes it)
controls.chat: Chat and commands (/help to see them). Ops (given in the server terminal with /op) have /gamemode, /tp, /give, /kill, /weather, /gamerule…; the admin also has /account, to create accounts
controls.pause: Pause (and close windows): Q and E change tab, 1–7 jump to one; the arrows or WASD move, Enter picks, and Esc or right click goes back. The shared world goes on meanwhile
controls.map.route: Mark a route to that point (near a house, the tavern or a place, it goes to its door) · remove it. A line on the ground and on the minimap leads you there, along roads where it can, and only through land you have explored. «Share the mark» sends it to the players with you; your partner sees your marks by themselves

social.say.greet_player: Hi, {name}! What are you up to?
npc.reply.greet.kind.friend: {name}! What a joy to see you!
npc.reply.greet.cheerful.friend: Well, {name}! So good to see you!
{name}! I was just thinking about you!
npc.reply.greet.shy.friend: Oh! Hi, {name}… nice to see you.
Hello, {name}. I saved you a smile.
npc.reply.greet.wry.friend: Look who it is! The best of the village.
{name}! Your usual's on the house. Almost.
Ah, {name}. One of the few who pay.
npc.reply.insult.kind.friend: Where did that come from? That hurt.
Oh dear. Bad day, is it?
npc.reply.insult.kind.neutral: Well, there's no need for that.
I'll pretend I didn't hear that.
npc.reply.insult.cheerful.friend: Ouch! Who are you and what did you do with my friend?
npc.reply.insult.cheerful.neutral: Well, someone got up on the wrong side of the bed!
npc.reply.insult.cheerful.cold: Go and be grumpy somewhere else!
npc.reply.insult.shy.friend: I… I thought we got along.
npc.reply.insult.shy.cold: Why are you always like this?
npc.reply.insult.gruff.friend: Watch it, {name}. I like you, but watch it.
Hmph. You'll take that back tomorrow.
npc.reply.insult.gruff.neutral: Say that again, I dare you!
npc.reply.insult.gruff.cold: Don't let me see you around here.
npc.reply.insult.wry.friend: I'll add that to your tab.
Is that how you thank your barman?
npc.reply.insult.wry.cold: I've thrown out better than you.
npc.reply.greet.rain: What weather, eh? The garden's happy, at least.
npc.reply.kid: Will you play with me later?
npc.witness.take: I saw that! Shame on you!
npc.witness.quarrel: In my day, people said hello.
npc.refuse: I've nothing to say to you.
People talk about you, you know.
npc.refuse.shop: Buy something or leave me be.
If you're buying, buy. If not, off you go.
npc.reproach: After what you said earlier? Hmph.
I'm still upset about before, you know.
You've got some nerve, after earlier.
npc.greet.warm: Hello, {name}! It's a pleasure having you in the village.
Hello, {name}! The village is lucky to have you.
npc.topic.weather_now.sol.kind: With this sun even the stones seem in a good mood.
npc.topic.weather_now.sol.cheerful: What light! It makes you want to do nothing useful all day.
npc.topic.weather_now.sol.shy: With this much light you don't know where to hide. It's nice, though.
npc.topic.weather_now.sol.gruff: Good day. I won't say it twice.
npc.topic.weather_now.sol.wry: Sunshine. The worst enemy of anyone who sells stew.
npc.topic.weather_now.sol.dani: In this sun green gets cocky! You have to calm it down with a bit of ochre.
npc.topic.weather_now.clear_night.kind: A clear night. I count the stars until they beat me.
npc.topic.weather_now.clear_night.gruff: Clear sky. Not one cloud to blame.
npc.topic.weather_now.clear_night.wry: You can see every star tonight. Not one of them has paid.
npc.topic.weather_now.clear_night: With a sky this clear, it's a pity to go in.
npc.topic.weather_now.nubes.kind: Clouds in no hurry. I like them: they promise nothing.
npc.topic.weather_now.nubes.cheerful: Cloudy, but the harmless kind. Works for me!
npc.topic.weather_now.nubes.shy: There's a cloud shaped like a carp… Well, there was.
npc.topic.weather_now.nubes.gruff: Cloudy. Not sun, not rain. Make up your mind.
npc.topic.weather_now.nubes.wry: The sky's wearing the face of someone who owes you money.
npc.topic.weather_now.lluvia.kind: Let it rain, let it rain: today the garden waters itself.
npc.topic.weather_now.lluvia.cheerful: Look at it pour! If anyone asks, my hair was already like this.
npc.topic.weather_now.lluvia.shy: I like listening to the rain… You don't need to talk so much.
npc.topic.weather_now.lluvia.gruff: Rain. At least it cleans the boots.
npc.topic.weather_now.lluvia.wry: It's raining. What a coincidence, just when you fancied staying for a drink.
npc.topic.weather_now.lluvia.lia: They bite sooner in the rain. It's not superstition: I've counted.
npc.topic.weather_now.lluvia.rosa: Nobody buys seeds in this weather, but nobody has to water either. Call it a draw.
npc.topic.weather_now.lluvia.eusebio: See? Rain. I say it every day, but today it counts.
npc.topic.weather_now.tormenta.kind: In a storm, what you want is a chair and someone beside you.
npc.topic.weather_now.tormenta.cheerful: What a racket! I'd say the sky is moving its furniture.
npc.topic.weather_now.tormenta.shy: I count the seconds until the thunder… It helps.
npc.topic.weather_now.tormenta.gruff: Storm. Keep away from tall trees and that's that.
npc.topic.weather_now.tormenta.wry: It's thundering so hard I can't hear the complaints. What a rest.
npc.topic.weather_now.tormenta.bruno: Thunder. At last, someone who hits harder than me.
npc.topic.weather_now.niebla.kind: In the fog the village looks like a dream that bothers no one.
npc.topic.weather_now.niebla.cheerful: You can't see a thing! Perfect day for hide-and-seek.
npc.topic.weather_now.niebla.shy: Fog… For a while nobody sees you. It's not so bad.
npc.topic.weather_now.niebla.wry: Fog. Today we're all gorgeous from a distance.
npc.topic.weather_now.niebla.ines: I don't go out measuring in fog. The whole map would come out blank.
npc.topic.weather_now.niebla.dani: Fog is the hardest white there is. And here I am, happily getting it wrong.
npc.topic.weather_now.nieve.kind: Snow hushes everything. Even the hens keep their voices down.
npc.topic.weather_now.nieve.cheerful: It's snowing! If a snowball flies by, it wasn't me.
npc.topic.weather_now.nieve.shy: Snow makes a very small sound when it falls… Almost none.
npc.topic.weather_now.nieve.wry: It's snowing. Today the fire is my best waiter.
npc.topic.weather_now.nieve.marta: Snowing, and me with wool to spare. What lovely weather.
npc.topic.weather_now.nieve.paco: The woods go still in the snow. You can hear the boar thinking.
npc.topic.forecast.sol.kind: Clear skies tomorrow. My knee hasn't said a word, and it always warns me.
npc.topic.forecast.sol.cheerful: It'll be fine tomorrow! I'll bet you anything. Well, something small.
npc.topic.forecast.sol.shy: It'll be clear tomorrow… I think. No: I know.
npc.topic.forecast.sol.gruff: Clear tomorrow. Make use of it.
npc.topic.forecast.sol.wry: Clear tomorrow. Not much of a story, I know.
npc.topic.forecast.nubes.kind: Clouds tomorrow and little else. A day for taking it slowly.
npc.topic.forecast.nubes.cheerful: Cloudy tomorrow, but no rain! No reason to put a hat on or take it off.
npc.topic.forecast.nubes.shy: There'll be clouds tomorrow… The kind that don't get you wet.
npc.topic.forecast.nubes.wry: Clouds tomorrow. Not even worth a complaint.
npc.topic.forecast.lluvia.kind: It'll rain tomorrow. That saves you the watering can.
npc.topic.forecast.lluvia.cheerful: Rain tomorrow! Find your hat. Or go without, it's more fun.
npc.topic.forecast.lluvia.shy: It'll rain tomorrow… You can feel it in the air. It smells of stone.
npc.topic.forecast.lluvia.gruff: Rain tomorrow. Get your outdoor jobs done today.
npc.topic.forecast.lluvia.wry: It'll rain tomorrow. I'll keep you a dry corner, just in case.
npc.topic.forecast.lluvia.lia: It'll rain tomorrow… And rain brings out the catfish, in the river and the lake.
npc.topic.forecast.lluvia.rosa: It'll rain tomorrow! If you've anything sown, don't even touch the watering can.
npc.topic.forecast.tormenta.kind: There's a storm coming tomorrow. Don't go too far, will you?
npc.topic.forecast.tormenta.cheerful: Thunder tomorrow! I've already picked the table I'll hide under.
npc.topic.forecast.tormenta.shy: There'll be a storm tomorrow… I always wait up for them.
npc.topic.forecast.tormenta.gruff: Storm tomorrow. If you go out, I don't want to hear about it.
npc.topic.forecast.tormenta.wry: Thunder tomorrow. The show is free; the chair, we'll see.
npc.topic.forecast.niebla.kind: Fog tomorrow. Slowly does it, and you'll get anywhere.
npc.topic.forecast.niebla.cheerful: Fog tomorrow! If you see a shape waving its arms, that's me.
npc.topic.forecast.niebla.shy: There'll be fog tomorrow… Best learn the way today.
npc.topic.forecast.niebla.gruff: Fog tomorrow. Stay on the path.
npc.topic.forecast.niebla.wry: Fog tomorrow. A great day to owe people money.
npc.topic.forecast.nieve.kind: It'll snow tomorrow. Bring your firewood in today, trust me.
npc.topic.forecast.nieve.cheerful: Snow tomorrow! Nobody step on the square before me!
npc.topic.forecast.nieve.shy: It's going to snow tomorrow… I'll get up early, to see it all untouched.
npc.topic.forecast.nieve.wry: Snow tomorrow. People will suddenly discover how nice it is in here.
npc.topic.forecast.unsure.kind: Tomorrow? It smells of something, but I can't say what.
npc.topic.forecast.unsure.cheerful: Tomorrow? No idea! It's more exciting that way.
npc.topic.forecast.unsure.shy: Tomorrow… I can't tell. I'd rather not say.
npc.topic.forecast.unsure.gruff: No idea about tomorrow. Look out and see.
npc.topic.forecast.unsure.wry: Tomorrow? If I knew, I'd charge for it.
npc.topic.forecast.always_rain.eusebio: It'll rain tomorrow. I say so every day, so take it for what it's worth.
Tomorrow? Rain. I've been saying it for forty years and some I got right.
I say rain. I always say rain. If you want the truth, ask Lía.
npc.topic.season_work.sow.rosa: Good weather for {crop, lower}: keep it watered, {n, plural, one {one day} other {about # days}} and into the basket.
With this weather I'd sow {crop, lower} today. And then I'd brag about it.
npc.topic.season_work.slow.rosa: {crop, The}, in this weather, at a donkey's pace: {n, plural, one {one day} other {about # days}} to the basket. And that's with watering.
You can sow {crop, lower}. But it's slow just now, mind. Water it and act natural.
npc.topic.season_work.cold.rosa: Still too chilly for {crop, the}. Sow now and the seed just waits. Like me for customers.
{crop, The}, once it warms up. Today the seed won't stir.
npc.topic.season_work.hot.rosa: Too hot for {crop, the}. That won't grow an inch today. Neither will I.
I wouldn't sow {crop, lower} in this heat: the seed just waits for it to cool down.
npc.topic.season_work.frost.rosa: Don't sow {crop, lower} today: it freezes tonight, and that's the end of the story.
The day fools you, but tonight it drops to {c} °C. {crop, The}, some other day.
npc.topic.season_work.frost_sown.rosa: It turns bitterly cold tonight. Look after {crop, the}: straw on the soil, or pick what's ready.
Got any straw for {crop, the}? It turns really cold tonight, and then come the tears at my stall.
npc.topic.season_work.wont.rosa: I wouldn't sow {crop, lower} now. With the weather that's coming, it won't reach the basket.
Sow {crop, lower} now? A wasted seed. And I make my living selling them.
npc.topic.season_work.none_sown.rosa: Right now I can't see {crop, lower} in any garden around here. I've got seeds, just saying.
No {crop, lower} in the ground, as far as I can see. And me with a drawer full of seeds.
npc.topic.season_work.grow.rosa: How are you doing with {crop, the}? Talk to the garden. I don't know if it helps, but it's company.
With {crop, the} in the ground, don't let the soil dry out. What doesn't drink doesn't grow.
npc.topic.season_work.no_crops.rosa: Nothing grows in this cold, so I sell flowerpots, bread and patience.
The soil's asleep now. Till it calmly: once it warms up it's all a rush.
With the soil this cold, I count the seeds so I don't get bored. I never get the same number.
npc.topic.season_work.fish.lia: In {water}, {fish, the} is biting. Well… when it feels like it.
If I could choose, I'd be at {water} now, after {fish, the}.
Have you tried for {fish, the}? At {water}. Now. And quietly.
npc.topic.season_work.ore.bruno: {item, The}: level {n} of the cave and below. Nothing before that.
Looking for {item, lower}? Level {n} or deeper. And light, plenty of light.
npc.topic.season_work.menu.anselmo: Today there's {item, lower}. Yesterday too, but today I say it with more feeling.
I recommend {item, the}. Not because it's the best: because it's the closest to hand.
npc.topic.season_work.clothes.marta: For this time of year, {item, a}. I sew while I listen: there's a bit of gossip in every seam.
At this time of year I'd get myself {item, a}. No obligation.
npc.topic.season_work.spring.nilo: In spring I get up before the hens. Just to annoy them a little.
npc.topic.season_work.summer.nilo: In summer, the nap is compulsory. It's written down somewhere.
npc.topic.season_work.autumn.nilo: Autumn and I are alike: we're slow, we creak and things fall off us.
npc.topic.season_work.winter.nilo: In winter the village shrinks and we all fit better.
npc.topic.season_work.spring.bruno: Spring: hoes. The same rush every year.
npc.topic.season_work.summer.bruno: In summer nobody comes near the forge. Good.
npc.topic.season_work.autumn.bruno: In autumn they bring me blunt axes. Then winter catches them by surprise.
npc.topic.season_work.winter.bruno: In winter the forge fills up. Suddenly everyone has a horseshoe to look at.
npc.topic.season_work.spring.dani: Spring uses up all my green! And I do stock up.
npc.topic.season_work.summer.dani: Summer is yellow. Not one yellow, though: forty.
npc.topic.season_work.autumn.dani: In autumn the trees compete with me. And they're winning.
npc.topic.season_work.winter.dani: Winter is white, grey and a little bit of red nose.
npc.topic.season_work.spring.anselmo: In spring everyone falls in love and nobody eats dinner. Ruinous.
npc.topic.season_work.summer.anselmo: Summer: they want everything cold. I draw the line at stew.
npc.topic.season_work.autumn.anselmo: In autumn people come back to the fire to tell last year's stories.
npc.topic.season_work.winter.anselmo: In winter I close at two, as always, and you'd think I was throwing them out of their own homes.
npc.topic.season_work.spring.eusebio: Short hair in spring. Don't say I didn't warn you.
npc.topic.season_work.summer.eusebio: In summer I cut twice as much. Hair, I mean. Conversation, the usual.
npc.topic.season_work.autumn.eusebio: In autumn hair falls out by itself. Bad time for the trade.
npc.topic.season_work.winter.eusebio: In winter everyone grows it long. It's warm, they say. So is a hat, and it comes off.
npc.topic.season_work.spring.ines: In spring I feel like going for a walk. Then I get to the door… and draw the door.
npc.topic.season_work.summer.ines: In summer the ink dries before I've decided where the river goes.
npc.topic.season_work.autumn.ines: In autumn the woods change colour and I have to open another inkwell.
npc.topic.season_work.winter.ines: In winter I draw from memory. That's why my winters come out so big.
npc.topic.season_work.spring.paco: In spring I don't shoot anything with young. I'm rough, but not that rough.
npc.topic.season_work.summer.paco: In summer, to the woods at dawn. At noon not even the shade hunts.
npc.topic.season_work.autumn.paco: Autumn belongs to the woods. Stay home and you stay smelling soup.
npc.topic.season_work.winter.paco: In winter I come back early and empty-handed. But what an appetite I bring.
npc.topic.season_work.spring.marta: In spring everyone wants out of long sleeves on the same day. The very same.
npc.topic.season_work.summer.marta: In summer I sew little and listen a lot. People talk more with bare arms.
npc.topic.season_work.autumn.marta: Autumn comes and out come all the worn elbows. They don't fool me: they're last year's.
npc.topic.season_work.winter.marta: In winter they ask me for a hat and end up telling me their life story. Same price.
npc.topic.season_work.spring.lia: In spring the water wakes up… You can see it in the colour.
npc.topic.season_work.summer.lia: In summer I put my feet in the pond and say I'm working.
npc.topic.season_work.autumn.lia: I like autumn. People go home and I stay with the water.
npc.topic.season_work.winter.lia: In winter I fish with gloves on… I don't catch anything, but what gloves.
npc.topic.their_day.plaza.nilo: I've a lot to do today: look at the square from here and think about looking at it from over there.
Here I am, on duty. Nobody asked me to, but someone has to.
Stay beside me a while and you'll find that nothing happens. It's wonderful.
npc.topic.their_day.work.rosa: I've sorted the seeds by colour. Nobody will find anything, but isn't it pretty.
The stall won't run itself. If only: I'd go to bed.
Ask, touch, look. I only charge for what you take.
npc.topic.their_day.pond.rosa: After the stall I come here to sell nothing to nobody. What a rest.
My legs fall asleep at the stall. I bring them here to wake up.
npc.topic.their_day.work.lia: I'm fishing… Well, I'm looking at the water with an excuse.
There's a huge carp living down there. I call her Madam. She hasn't answered.
If you talk quietly, you can stay.
npc.topic.their_day.plaza.lia: I come to the square for a bit of people. Just a little. Then, water.
Rosa says I should socialise. There: I've seen you.
npc.topic.their_day.work.bruno: Can't put this down now. Talk, I'm listening. More or less.
Red-hot iron, a hammer and patience. That's the whole secret.
npc.topic.their_day.board.bruno: I come to read the board. Lots of asking and not much please.
I shut the forge and stretch my back. Sounds just like the anvil.
npc.topic.their_day.work.dani: Don't look yet! …All right, look. How's the duck?
The pond won't keep still today. How is anyone supposed to work?
npc.topic.their_day.plaza.dani: I'm looking for a face to paint. I know Nilo's by heart.
I come to the square to steal colours. I give them back later, in the painting.
npc.topic.their_day.work.anselmo: I've had this cloth in my hand since I opened. The bar's no different, but I feel better.
Here, serving. There are worse jobs. Drinking what I serve, for one.
Ask whatever you like. I charge for answers by size.
npc.topic.their_day.tavern.eusebio: Waiting for customers. That's the barber's chair; the stool is mine.
I cut hair, give my opinion and go back to my stool. In that order.
npc.topic.their_day.tavern.ines: I'm making a fair copy of a coastline… That's what the cider's for: the waves.
People here tell you where they've been. I draw it, and then they're embarrassed.
npc.topic.their_day.tavern.marta: I've put down my needles for today. Now it's my tongue's turn: it doesn't prick.
I sit at this table because you can see who comes in, and with what face.
npc.topic.their_day.tavern.paco: From the woods to the chair. It's the part of the day I'm best at.
Beer and quiet. With you here, I don't see the second one happening.
npc.topic.their_day.road: I'm off {goal}, but I've a moment for you.
I was going {goal}. I'll stop: if I walk and talk I trip.
npc.topic.their_day.road.cheerful: You've caught me going {goal}! Tell me something, quick.
npc.topic.their_day.road.shy: I was going {goal}… But there's no hurry.
npc.topic.hour.early.nilo: At this hour only the hens and I are up. And they complain.
Getting up early is no use at all, but how peaceful.
npc.topic.hour.early.lia: At this hour the water doesn't know yet that you're watching.
Good… Sorry, I hadn't spoken to anyone yet today.
npc.topic.hour.early.bruno: Early. Good. Iron doesn't wait either.
npc.topic.hour.early: What an early start. The village is still half dressed.
npc.topic.hour.late.nilo: At my age you sleep little. I dream awake, it's less tiring.
Night is for owls and old men. And, look, for you too.
npc.topic.hour.late.eusebio: It's late. If I get up, the stool will go cold.
npc.topic.hour.late.anselmo: At this hour nobody lies any more: they haven't the brains left.
The one-in-the-morning crowd is the best. And the worst. It's the same crowd.
npc.topic.hour.late.marta: The best stories come when you can't see the needle any more.
I should go home. I say it every night, at this hour, in this chair.
npc.topic.hour.late.paco: At night the woods belong to others. I belong to the beer.
npc.topic.likes.kind: Don't tell anyone, but for {some, the} I'd even get up from my nap.
You know what cheers me up any day? {some}. It's that easy.
npc.topic.likes.cheerful: I'd do anything for {some, lower}! We all have our vices.
I'll tell you a secret: if you see me smiling for no reason, {some, lower} must be involved.
npc.topic.likes.shy: Something I like… No, you'll laugh. {some}.
If you ever don't know what to do with some {some, lower}… Never mind. Or do. Do mind.
npc.topic.likes.gruff: I don't ask for anything. Mind you, if we're talking about {some, lower}, I won't say no.
npc.topic.likes.wry: Everyone has a price. Mine: {some, lower}.
If you want me to like you, bring {some, lower}. It's cheaper than a round of drinks.
npc.topic.wish.nilo: Know what I miss? {item, The} from when the village had a bakery.
Last night I dreamt of {item, a}. I woke up looking for the crumbs.
npc.topic.wish.rosa: I've had a craving for days: {some, lower}. And not a trace of it at my own stall.
If the world were fair, there'd be {some, lower} for tea today.
npc.topic.wish.lia: I'd love to have {item, a} in front of me… Even just for a little while.
Sometimes I think about {item, the}… and the afternoon's gone.
npc.topic.wish.bruno: I haven't seen {item, a} up close in years. Years.
If you come across {item, a}, think of me. That's all I'll say.
npc.topic.wish.dani: I've a half-finished painting. Know what it needs? {item, A}. No more, no less.
I'd give my best brush for {item, a}. Well, my second best.
npc.topic.wish.anselmo: I serve everyone and nobody serves me. And me so fond of {item, the}.
If someone served me {item, lower} tonight, I'd pretend it wasn't my kitchen.
npc.topic.wish.eusebio: My mother used to make {item, lower}. Nobody's got it right since, and I've tried plenty.
{item, The}. That's all I ask. That, and rain.
npc.topic.wish.ines: If I had {item, a}… I don't know. I'd draw better, surely.
I'm embarrassed to say it, but… {item, a}. I'd really like that.
npc.topic.wish.marta: As a girl I used to have {some, lower} on our doorstep. I haven't for ages.
With {some, lower} in front of me I go quiet for a while. Imagine how much I like it.
npc.topic.wish.paco: All this hunting and not one decent {item, lower}. Months I've been like this.
I burn everything. {item, The} cooked by someone else: now that's eating.
npc.topic.request.kind: I'm asking you because I trust you: {what}. It's on the board.
I've put a little note on the board: {what}. No pressure… but today.
npc.topic.request.cheerful: Hey! You wouldn't have {what} lying around? It's on the board, and I pay well.
Wanted, in any condition: {what}! Reward on the board.
npc.topic.request.shy: On the board I've asked for… {what}. If you can. If not, it's fine.
I'm embarrassed to ask, so I wrote it on the board: {what}.
npc.topic.request.gruff: I need {what}. It's on the board, but if you bring it, hand it to me and done.
My note on the board: {what}. I don't ask twice a day.
npc.topic.request.wry: There's a note of mine on the board: {what}. Read it in a sad voice, it works better.
npc.topic.your_place.perro: How's {animal}? Give that back a scratch from me.
{animal} has a better temper than half the village. I won't say which half.
npc.topic.your_place.perro.paco: In the woods I'd get more use out of a dog like {animal} than out of my brother-in-law.
npc.topic.your_place.gato: And {animal}? Cats are the only ones who know how to live.
They say the cat runs the house. {animal} would agree.
npc.topic.your_place.gato.lia: {animal} and I want the same thing from the pond… But I let it go.
npc.topic.your_place.caballo: How's {animal} behaving? With a horse like that, everything's close.
Brush {animal} now and then. You'll get it back at a gallop.
npc.topic.your_place.caballo.bruno: Is {animal} wearing my horseshoes? You can tell at a gallop.
npc.topic.your_place.hens: You've got {n} hens, haven't you? That's a lot of opinions in one place.
npc.topic.your_place.hens.nilo: Don't argue with your hens. There are {n} of them and they're right.
npc.topic.your_place.farm: You're up to {n} animals. Do you know all their names?
With {n} animals to look after, getting up early stops being a virtue.
npc.topic.your_place.farm.rosa: {n} animals already? Who does your feed accounts?
npc.topic.your_place.big: Had the house made bigger, eh? Careful: the more room, the more clutter.
npc.topic.your_place.big.nilo: How's the house, now it's bigger? I go past it often. In my thoughts.
npc.topic.your_place.family: A family house, no less. Now you'll have to fill it with noise.
In a house like that, the hard part is finding your slippers.
npc.topic.your_place.family.nilo: That family house is the best thing I ever built sitting down.
npc.topic.your_family.expecting: Got a name yet? They arrive and you have to call them something.
A baby on the way… Sleep now, because later you won't be allowed to.
npc.topic.your_family.expecting.marta: When it's born I want to be the first to know. Well, the second: nobody beats Rosa.
npc.topic.your_family.baby: Does {kid} let you sleep? No need to answer.
With a baby at home time runs backwards. Give {kid} a kiss.
npc.topic.your_family.baby.nilo: When {kid} grows up, come to the square together. I'll teach the art of doing nothing with style.
npc.topic.your_family.kid: How's {kid}? At that age they grow between one hello and the next.
{kid} asks more questions than a tax collector. Just answer, that's how they learn.
npc.topic.your_family.kid.nilo: {kid} and I have a deal: I tell stories and {ksex, select, girl {she} other {he}} pretends to believe them.
npc.topic.your_family.kid.dani: {kid} can borrow my brushes any time! The old ones.
npc.topic.your_family.kid.lia: {kid} can come fishing with me… You have to keep quiet, though.
npc.chat.nilo.personal: I had a sweetheart who went to see the sea and sent me a letter: "It's very big". I never knew if that was good or bad.
When I was young I wanted to leave. I got to the first crossroads and sat down to think about it… | And here I am, still thinking.
When I'm gone, hold a minute's nap for me. Not silence: that drags on.
Before you came, that house at the end of the path had been dark for years. I said good night to it all the same.
npc.chat.rosa.personal: The stall was my mother's. She sold without saying a word. I don't know who I take after.
Sometimes I'm afraid Lía will row off and not come back. Don't tell her, she'd laugh.
Once I closed the stall for a whole day, to rest. | By eleven I was at home sorting the larder by size.
I wanted to be a singer. Then I heard myself.
npc.chat.lia.personal: As a girl I fell in the pond and Rosa pulled me out by the hair. I owe her one. She says two.
I talk more to fish than to people… Fish don't ask you what's wrong.
I keep a notebook of what bites and when. Rosa writes the shopping in it.
If I go far away one day, it'll be slowly, rowing. And I'll come back to tell it… quietly.
npc.chat.bruno.personal: My father was a smith too. He never said a thing was good. He said: "it'll do".
Once a whole grille came out crooked and I left it. They say it's art. It's a mistake.
I don't sleep much. After the hammer, silence is too loud.
I had an apprentice. He left for the coast. I gave him the good hammer. Don't tell.
npc.chat.dani.personal: I came here knowing nobody. The first day Nilo asked me if I knew how to nap. I knew I was staying.
The pink hair was an accident with a pigment. Now it's a decision.
My family wanted me to be a notary. Can you see me as a notary? I'd sign in glitter.
Sometimes I paint a whole picture over in white and start again. | Under the duck there's a bridge. And under the bridge, another duck.
npc.chat.anselmo.personal: I inherited the tavern, the debts and a ladle. The ladle's the only one that's never let me down.
They think I listen out of politeness. I listen so I can tell it later. But yours I keep.
I nearly got married. She asked me to close on Sundays. | Sundays are very lively here.
Before I open I have a bowl of broth, all alone. It's my moment. Don't tell Marta, she'd come.
npc.chat.eusebio.personal: I had a barbershop with a pole at the door. Then I saw the customers were in here, so I brought the chair.
The first time I cut Nilo's hair was at school. Without permission.
My sister-in-law says I live in the tavern. She exaggerates. I sleep elsewhere.
As a boy I missed the fair because of the rain. | Since then I announce it every day. That way I'm disappointed in advance.
npc.chat.ines.personal: The first map I made was of my bedroom. I got the door wrong.
Roads don't scare me. Asking for directions does.
My father carried the post and got lost. I'd draw where I thought he was. | I was nearly always wrong, but we slept better at home.
I'm keeping one sheet blank. It's for when I find a place I like more than this stool.
npc.chat.marta.personal: I learned to knit to have somewhere to look while I listened. I no longer know which came first.
My husband was a sailor. He left a jumper half done and I finished it. I don't like leaving things half done.
Secrets? The good ones I keep. The others I tell with a different name.
One winter I knitted a scarf so long it did for three. | Anselmo, Eusebio and I wore it first. We had to go everywhere together.
npc.chat.paco.personal: My brother-in-law says he once caught a deer with his hands. The deer tells it differently.
Once I had a boar in my sights and it looked at me. I lowered the bow. Don't tell my brother-in-law.
In the woods I never get lost. At parties, always.
On days I bring nothing I stay out a bit longer, so it looks like I tried. | I did try, mind.
npc.opinion.nilo.rosa: Rosa sells so charmingly that I once bought fertilizer. I don't have a garden.
npc.opinion.nilo.bruno: Bruno growls, but he fixed my cane and wouldn't take a coin.
npc.opinion.nilo.dani: Dani asked me what colour my soul is. I said checked, like my blanket.
npc.opinion.nilo.eusebio: Eusebio and I have been arguing since school. We've forgotten what about, but we're not stopping now.
npc.opinion.rosa.lia: Lía's up before the fish and I'm up before the customers. At home we don't even meet to argue.
npc.opinion.rosa.bruno: Bruno pays the exact amount. Counted twice. Under his breath.
npc.opinion.rosa.marta: No surprise survives Marta. You tell her to get advice and it's everyone's.
npc.opinion.rosa.dani: Dani asked me to pose with a turnip! I told him the turnip is extra.
npc.opinion.lia.rosa: Rosa talks in her sleep… About prices.
npc.opinion.lia.nilo: Nilo says hello quietly so as not to scare the fish. That's thoughtful, isn't it?
npc.opinion.lia.ines: Inés and I once talked for a whole hour. Well… we were there an hour. It was lovely.
npc.opinion.lia.dani: Dani paints the pond and I try not to move the water. It's teamwork.
npc.opinion.bruno.paco: Paco brings me bent arrows and says it was the wind. The wind.
npc.opinion.bruno.dani: Dani asked me for a pretty nail. A nail. Pretty.
npc.opinion.bruno.anselmo: Anselmo says I owe him a round. He keeps the tally. Nothing to be done.
npc.opinion.dani.bruno: Bruno has the best hands in the village to paint! He won't let me.
npc.opinion.dani.nilo: Nilo keeps so still he's the perfect model. Then it turns out he was asleep.
npc.opinion.dani.marta: Marta and I start out talking about colours and end up talking about people. Always.
npc.opinion.dani.lia: Lía has a blue in her eyes I can't mix. I've used up half my palette.
npc.opinion.anselmo.eusebio: Eusebio's had that stool for years. One day I'll charge rent and he'll die of shock. Or pay, which would be worse.
npc.opinion.anselmo.paco: Paco brings the hunger of three wolves and the catch of half a rabbit.
npc.opinion.anselmo.marta: Marta doesn't repeat gossip: she improves it.
npc.opinion.anselmo.ines: Inés asked me to put out a candle so she could see north better. I didn't ask.
npc.opinion.eusebio.anselmo: Anselmo's bald. What we have is friendship, not business.
npc.opinion.eusebio.nilo: Nilo was already napping at school. It's the one thing he got good marks in.
npc.opinion.eusebio.paco: No comb can handle Paco's curls. There are leaves in there from last year.
npc.opinion.eusebio.bruno: Bruno shaves his own head. With what, I'd rather not know.
npc.opinion.ines.lia: Lía knows the water without a map… I'm a little envious.
npc.opinion.ines.anselmo: Anselmo keeps this seat for me. I never asked… That's why I come.
npc.opinion.ines.paco: Paco points out paths with his chin. It's hard to draw.
npc.opinion.ines.dani: Dani paints the sea purple and they say how lovely. I bend a river by a finger… and they write to me.
npc.opinion.marta.dani: Have you seen Dani paint? Three days he's been on the same duck. It's a very handsome duck.
npc.opinion.marta.anselmo: Anselmo boasts he never hears a thing. I keep him informed, so we both lie less.
npc.opinion.marta.rosa: Rosa and I tell each other everything. Then we act surprised.
npc.opinion.marta.bruno: I mended Bruno's apron and he thanked me with his head. Like this: an inch.
npc.opinion.paco.eusebio: Eusebio's wanted to cut my hair since the first day I walked in. That's why I sit far away.
npc.opinion.paco.bruno: Bruno makes good arrowheads. That I miss isn't his doing.
npc.opinion.paco.marta: Marta asked me what this stain was. The woods, I said.
npc.opinion.paco.anselmo: Anselmo roasts what I bring and says he saved it. Maybe he did.
npc.greet.morning.kind: Good morning, {name}. Easy now, the day is long.
npc.greet.morning.cheerful: Morning! I was dying for someone to come by!
Good morning, {name}! You're not leaving without telling me something.
npc.greet.morning.shy: Oh, {name}. Good morning… You're the first thing I've said today.
npc.greet.morning.wry: Good morning, or whatever this is.
npc.greet.day.kind: Hello, {name}. It's good to see your face.
npc.greet.day.cheerful: {name}! Come here, I've things to tell you.
Hello! You've caught me arguing with nobody, and I was losing.
npc.greet.day.shy: Oh, {name}… Hello. I was miles away.
Hello. I saw you coming, so I had time to think of it: hello.
npc.greet.day.wry: {name}, what an honour. Here to spend or to look?
Well, {name}. Just as I was about to rest from doing nothing.
npc.greet.evening.kind: Good evening, {name}. Was it a good day's work?
npc.greet.evening.cheerful: Hello! I've used up my day, but tell me about yours.
npc.greet.evening.shy: Hello, {name}. It's easier to talk at this hour… More quietly.
npc.greet.evening.gruff: Evening, {name}. I'm not up to much, but speak.
npc.greet.evening.wry: About time, {name}. I'd started talking to the barrels.
npc.greet.night.kind: Good evening, {name}. Can't sleep? Me neither.
npc.greet.night.shy: Hello, {name}. I was about to leave… But only about to.
npc.greet.night.wry: Good evening, {name}. The last one. Or the one before, it's luckier.
npc.greet.rain: What weather… But the garden's grateful.
npc.greet.snow: I love the way snow crunches.
npc.mood.low.kind: Hello, {name}. Even my memories feel heavy today.
Forgive me if I don't say much. Some days are like that.
npc.mood.low.cheerful: I got up on someone else's wrong foot today. Hello, anyway.
Hi. If I don't laugh today, it's not you, all right?
npc.mood.low.shy: I haven't many words today… Sorry.
Hello… Do you mind if we talk softly?
npc.mood.low.gruff: Today's not the day. But go on.
Hm. I'm in a foul mood. It's not you.
npc.mood.low.wry: Today not even my own jokes are funny. Imagine everyone else's.
Hello. Today I'm smiling inside. Very deep inside.
npc.mood.high.kind: {name}! Nothing hurts today. Suspicious, but I'm enjoying it.
I was already having a good day, and now here you are.
npc.mood.high.cheerful: {name}! Everything's going right today! Touch wood, just in case.
Hello, hello! Nobody can stop me today. Well, you just did.
npc.mood.high.shy: Hello, {name}. Today… I'm happy. I don't know why.
I felt like talking to someone today. I'm glad it's you.
npc.mood.high.gruff: Afternoon. Yes, I'm in a good mood. Keep it to yourself.
npc.mood.high.wry: {name}! Today I'd almost give you credit. Almost.
I'm in such a good mood I've swept the floor.
npc.mood.extra.kind: It's a pleasure talking with you, truly.
npc.mood.extra.cheerful: Come back later, I've got more!
npc.mood.extra.wry: If anyone asks, this was a serious conversation.
npc.intro.rosa: You must be {name}! I'm Rosa, from the stall. Seeds, hens and conversation. The last one's free.
npc.intro.lia: Oh… Hello. I'm Lía. I fish. You're… {name}? I'll remember. I'm better with fish, but I'll remember.
npc.intro.bruno: Bruno. From the forge. {name}? Good. If something breaks, I'm there. If you just want to talk, too. But not much.
npc.intro.dani: Hi! I'm Dani, I paint things. Ducks, mostly. And you're {name}? What a great title for a painting!
npc.intro.anselmo: Anselmo, at your service. Not a figure of speech: it's the job. And you're {name}. Around here names arrive before people do.
npc.intro.eusebio: Eusebio. Barber. Your hair and I will have words. {name}? Well, it's going to rain, {name}. I always say so.
npc.intro.ines: Hello… Inés. I make maps. {name}? I'll note you in the margin, next to the village.
npc.intro.marta: I'm Marta, dear: I sew, I knit and I ask. I'll start: you're {name}, aren't you? I knew it.
npc.intro.paco: Paco. I hunt. Well, I go to the woods. And you? …{name}. Right. Sit, if you like. Or don't.
npc.intro.kind: I don't think we've met. I'm {npc}. {name}? What a pleasure, truly.
npc.intro.cheerful: A new face! I'm {npc}. And you? {name}! I like it.
npc.intro.wry: {npc}, and the rumours are true. {name}, isn't it? Yours, we'll see.
npc.gift.loved.kind: {item}? Oh, I'm moved. Thank you, {name}. With all my heart.
npc.gift.loved.cheerful: {item}?! It's my favourite thing in the whole world!
npc.gift.loved.shy: Oh… {item, lower}. How did you know? Thank you. Thank you so much.
npc.gift.loved.gruff: {item}. …Give me a moment. There's something in my eye.
npc.gift.loved.wry: {item}. And there I was, boasting that nothing impresses me. Thank you.
npc.gift.liked.kind: What a lovely thought. Just what I fancied.
npc.gift.liked.cheerful: Oh, I love it! Thank you, really.
npc.gift.liked.shy: I like it a lot… Thank you, {name}.
npc.gift.liked.wry: Well, someone pays attention. Much obliged.
npc.gift.neutral.shy: Oh… Thank you. You needn't have.
npc.gift.neutral.gruff: Thanks. I'll find a use for it.
npc.gift.neutral.wry: Thanks. One should never look at the price of a gift. I already have.
npc.gift.hated.kind: Ah… Well. It's the thought that counts, isn't it?
npc.gift.hated.cheerful: Is this… for me? Ah. Right. Thanks… I guess.
npc.gift.hated.shy: Oh… Is it for me? Are you sure?
npc.gift.hated.gruff: Not this. But, well, what's given is given.
npc.gift.hated.wry: Very funny. I'll find someone to pass it on to.
npc.gift.again.kind: {item} again? You'll spoil me. Thank you.
npc.gift.again.cheerful: {item} again! I almost expected it. Thanks all the same!
npc.gift.again.shy: Oh, {item, lower}… Like last time. Thank you.
npc.gift.again.wry: {item}. Again. I'm starting to see a pattern.
npc.thanks.kind: Thank you so much! I owe you one. Well, I owe you this:
npc.thanks.cheerful: You've saved my day! Here, as promised:
npc.thanks.shy: You really brought it? Thank you… This is yours:
npc.thanks.gruff: You deliver. That's how I like it. Here:
npc.thanks.wry: Quick and no questions asked. Here's yours:
npc.wish.kept.kind: You remembered! I won't forget this, {name}.
npc.wish.kept.cheerful: You remembered! I said it once and you remembered!
npc.wish.kept.shy: It was… exactly that. You remembered. I don't know what to say.
npc.wish.kept.gruff: I only said it for something to say. And you go and bring it. …Thanks, {name}.
npc.wish.kept.wry: I say a lot of things and nobody remembers them. Until today.
npc.recall.wish_kept: I said there was something I wished for, and you turned up with it. I can't stop thinking about it, {name}.
It still makes me happy to think of {item, the} you brought me.

npc.trade.ask: What would you like? Each trade can be made a few times a day.
npc.nilo.first: So you're {name}! At last someone's come to the house at the end of the path. It had been empty for years.
This is Pueblo Brotes. Small, yes, but here everyone builds their life their own way.

I've left you some iron tools: axe, pickaxe, scythe, hoe and shovel. Pick them with the number keys and use them with the left click. To use anything else, get close, put the cursor on it and press E.
Don't worry, you needn't know everything today. I've written down what to do, one thing at a time, at the top left.
npc.nilo.reform: By the way, that house is going to feel small. With 40 planks and 30 stones I'll make it bigger: more room for furniture.
npc.nilo.later: All right, I'll gather it and come back
npc.nilo.reform.done: Done! Pass me the hammer… I mean, it's finished. Your house is much bigger now. Go and see it.
npc.nilo.family: If the family's going to grow, you need room. With 80 planks, 60 stones and 6 iron ingots I'll build you a family house: bedroom, children's room, bathroom, kitchen and living room. You bring the furniture.
npc.nilo.family.done: Done! You've got a family house. Build the double bed, the cot, the children's beds and the kitchen and bathroom things with B (I sell the plans for the beds and the cot; Dani, the rest), and set it up as you like.

npc.chat.nilo.misc: When I was young this village even had a bakery. And a dog called Bread.
The secret of a good life: take a nap and don't argue with the hens.
Have you seen that sky? Tomorrow it'll rain, or it won't. Eighty years and I still can't get it right.
I'm glad that house at the end of the path has people again. An empty house gets sad.
npc.events.nilo.3: You know, my grandfather said that if you keep walking west, you end up coming back from the east. That the world goes round.
Nobody has ever checked. But if anyone can, it's you. Here, this was his.
npc.events.nilo.6: You've become someone important to this village. And to this old man.
Have this pie. I made it. Well, Rosa made it, but I watched a lot.
npc.chat.rosa.misc: Fresh seeds, get your fresh seeds! Well, fresh… from this year. Almost all.
My sister Lía spends all day fishing. I spend all day selling what she doesn't catch.
Sow tomatoes, let it freeze that night, and the plant gets cross and never speaks to you again. Like me without coffee.
They say that if you sing while you water, things grow faster. I haven't tried: I sing terribly.
npc.events.rosa.3: Listen, you're one of my best customers. From today, everything's a bit cheaper for you.
And don't tell Bruno, or they'll all want a discount!
npc.events.rosa.6: Here, the guest bed. I don't get guests any more: Lía snores.
npc.chat.lia.misc: Did you know eels hardly come out before dark? Like owls. And like my sister when there's cake.
The goldfish exists. I saw it once. Well, I dreamt it. But very hard.
In the sea there are sardines and sea bass; in the rivers, trout, and salmon in autumn.
With a boat you could reach islands nobody has set foot on. I sell the plans, by the way.
npc.events.lia.3: Here, some good fishing line. It'll hold bigger fish.
npc.events.lia.6: I saw a sunken ship on the coast, far to the south. They say there's a chest inside. Do you dare?
npc.chat.bruno.misc: Hitting hot metal is the most relaxing thing in the world. After sleeping.
In the caves, the deeper you go, the better the stones. And the more beasts. Take torches.
A sword isn't for fighting: it's so the beasts think twice.
Iron takes a copper pickaxe. Gold takes an iron one. That's how it is.
npc.events.bruno.3: Here, some ingots I had to spare. I didn't have them to spare, but they're yours anyway.
npc.events.bruno.6: I forged this sword years ago, for myself. Now it's yours. Look after it.
npc.chat.dani.misc: I'm painting the pond. Three days on the same duck.
This village's favourite colour is green. I counted.
Thank you for the new house. It smells of wood and of the future.
If you find gemstones in the caves, bring them to me: I make paint out of them.
npc.events.dani.3: I've painted you. Well, I've painted your shadow. Have a flowerpot, I've plenty.
npc.events.dani.6: You're my muse. I'm not joking. Here, a rug I wove by hand.
npc.chat.anselmo.misc: The usual? Whatever you say, I'm giving you the usual.
Here we know everything before it happens. Rosa's already told me what you'll do tomorrow.
The beer recipe was my grandmother's. So was the stew. My grandmother couldn't cook.
If you don't pay today, you pay tomorrow. And if not, I'll tell Bruno you owe me money.
More troubles have been sorted out at this bar than in the whole town hall. Well, there's no town hall.
npc.events.anselmo.3: You're one of us now. Here, this one's on me. Don't tell anyone, I've a reputation.
npc.events.anselmo.6: Take this stool. It was my father's. He doesn't use it any more: he says his legs have grown.
npc.chat.eusebio.misc: I've been on this stool since before there was a tavern.
Think it's going to rain? I think so. I say it every day and sometimes I'm right.
Nilo and I went to school together. He was already old then.
They say there's ice up north that never ends. I haven't gone to look: it's far from my stool.
npc.events.eusebio.3: Here, from my garden. Well, from my sister-in-law's garden. Well, she doesn't know.
npc.chat.ines.misc: I'm a cartographer. Well, I paint things and say it's the world.
I've been in a temple that isn't on any map. Not on mine either: I forgot the paper.
If you're travelling, take torches. And a map. And torches.
They say if you keep walking straight, you come back here. So I stop sooner: I'm already here.
npc.events.ines.3: Here, a blank map. What matters is what you put on it.
npc.chat.marta.misc: I come here to be told things. Anselmo makes them up, but he tells them very well.
I spend all day knitting. In the evening I rest my hands and exercise my tongue.
The cider here takes away your sorrows. They come back later, but by then they're tired.
You come here for the stew and stay for what you hear.
npc.events.marta.3: I've made you a hat. I know you didn't ask. That's why it's a present.
npc.chat.paco.misc: I hunt. Well, I go to the woods and sometimes I come back with something.
You have to crouch to get near a deer. Walk upright and they'll hear you in the next village.
The boar is clever. Cleverer than my brother-in-law, which isn't hard either.
From the hide you make leather, from the leather, boots. And with the boots, off hunting again.
npc.events.paco.3: Here, from the last thing I hunted. Roasted by Anselmo: I burn everything.
npc.chat.nilo.tip: They say the world never ends beyond the forest. I've never gone that far.
The big boulders have everything: stone, coal, copper, iron and sometimes gold. But your pickaxe wears out: look after it.
They say that in the mountains the boulders hide more iron and more gold.
A furnace turns ore into ingots. And with copper ingots, an anvil for forging. If a tool breaks, you make another there, or buy it from Bruno.
In the kitchen, a roast apple fills you twice as much as a raw one. Trust me.
If you run out of coal, burn wood in the furnace. That's how my grandfather did it.
In the tavern, west of the path, Anselmo feeds you and tells you everyone's life. Mostly the second.
The palms on the warm beaches give coconuts every few days. No need to fell them: a shake will do.
A waterwheel on a river grinds wheat into flour and waters the garden around it by itself. With flour, bread comes cheaper.
Dig five blocks down with the shovel and, with the stonecutter's table nearby, you can make a well: water for your can without going to the river.
rep.title: Reputation in Pueblo Brotes
rep.level.outcast.desc: The neighbors avoid you: they won't chat (unless you're good friends), though the shops and the trades stay open. Gifts make peace.
rep.level.distrusted.desc: People look at you sideways: the shops charge you more and the friendship moments wait.
rep.level.newcomer.desc: Hardly anyone knows you yet. Do errands, greet people, bring gifts.
rep.level.known.desc: People know your face and say hello.
rep.level.liked.desc: The village likes you: the shops treat you a little better.
rep.level.beloved.desc: Everyone loves you: the best prices, and a friend in every house.
rep.creative: In creative mode the reputation doesn't change.
rep.why.take_seen: Taking from a house in front of a neighbor
rep.why.knock_night: Knocking on a door at night

farm.almanac.help: Crops grow by the warmth and the water of each day: a watered bed lasts about two days in summer, three in spring and autumn and many in winter; seedlings want it more often. Frost kills the tender ones and four mornings without water kill any (on days nobody plays they only wilt). Ripe crops pass: roots go to seed and fruits rot, and both leave seeds. With the scythe, wheat gives straw too: on the soil it keeps the water in. Seeds are made by hand (C).

npc.remark.carcass: Goodness, what a beast! Mind the blood on my stall.
That'll feed a family for a week.
Good hunting, {name}! Don't drip on the path.
Heavy load, eh? Off to the kitchen with it.
npc.remark.log: Carrying a whole tree, are we?
Mind your back with that log, {name}.
npc.remark.blood: Is that blood? Tell me it's not yours.
You look like you've come from the butcher's.
{name}, you've got blood all over your shirt!
Go and wash that off before you scare the children.
npc.remark.soaked: You're dripping, {name}! Get out of the rain.
Did you fall in the river?
Dry off before you catch a cold.
Look at you, wet to the bone!
npc.remark.snowy: You've got snow on your shoulders!
Shake that snow off, {name}, or you'll freeze.
Snow on your head... come and warm up.
npc.remark.muddy: Mind your boots, you're leaving a trail.
That mud goes right up to your knees!
Wipe your feet before you go in anywhere.
npc.remark.filthy: Hard day's work, I can tell.
{name}, when did you last see a bathtub?
You've got half the farm on you.
A good wash wouldn't hurt, you know.
npc.remark.torn: Your clothes are coming apart at the seams.
Those elbows have seen better days, {name}.
Marta could mend that for you.
Holes in your clothes? Winter won't forgive that.
npc.remark.underwear: I'll pretend I didn't see anything.
npc.remark.barefoot: You'll get splinters walking like that.
Ah, feeling the earth, are we?
npc.remark.underdressed: Go and put something warm on.
Your lips are blue! Come by the fire.
npc.remark.overdressed: Take that coat off before you faint!
npc.remark.haircut: That cut takes years off you.
npc.remark.new_clothes: I like that! Where did you get it?
npc.remark.couple: Out for a walk together? How lovely.
{name}, you two make a fine pair.
npc.remark.wrapped_up: Good coat, {name}. Sensible, in this weather.
Now that's how you dress for the snow.
You won't feel the cold in that, I bet.
npc.remark.carcass.kind: Oh my, what a catch! Don't strain yourself.
Well done, {name}. Mind the blood, dear.
npc.remark.carcass.cheerful: Wow! Is that for dinner? Invite me!
What a beast, {name}! That's real hunting!
npc.remark.carcass.shy: Oh! That poor... um, nice catch.
B-blood... I'll look the other way.
npc.remark.carcass.gruff: Don't drip that on my doorstep, {name}.
npc.remark.carcass.wry: Lovely. Now the whole village smells of the hunt.
npc.remark.filthy.kind: You've worked so hard, {name}. A warm bath will do you good.
Goodness, look at you! Go and wash, dear.
npc.remark.filthy.cheerful: Ha! You look like you wrestled a pig!
npc.remark.filthy.gruff: Wash before you touch anything of mine.
npc.remark.filthy.wry: Is that a new fashion? Very... earthy.
{name}, the pigs want their mud back.
npc.remark.soaked.kind: You're soaked through, {name}! Come and dry off.
Oh dear, you'll catch a cold. Find a fire.
npc.remark.soaked.cheerful: Ha! You look like a drowned cat, {name}!
npc.remark.soaked.wry: Swimming in your clothes? Bold choice.
npc.remark.fresh.kind: You smell lovely, {name}. Like clean linen.
Fresh as a daisy! It does you good.
npc.remark.fresh.cheerful: Mmm, soap! Is it a special day?
npc.remark.fresh.wry: Did you get lost and end up in a bathtub?
npc.remark.torn.kind: Your poor clothes, {name}. Marta could mend them.
Those holes will let the cold in, dear.
npc.remark.torn.cheerful: Ooh, holes! Is that the fashion now?
Your clothes have been through the wars, {name}!
npc.recall.gift_loved: I still think about {item, the} you gave me. Thank you, {name}.
Remember {item, the} you brought me? Wonderful.
{item, The} you gave me... what a treat that was.
npc.recall.gift_hated: About {item, the} you gave me... let's not talk about it.
I haven't forgotten {item, the}, {name}. And not in a good way.
I'm still trying to forget {item, the} you gave me.
npc.recall.insult: I haven't forgotten what you said to me, {name}.
You were quite rude to me the other day.
npc.recall.take_seen: I saw what you did, {name}. I haven't forgotten.
Keep your hands where I can see them.
Some people don't know what's theirs and what isn't.
npc.recall.helped: Thank you again for your help, {name}.
You got me out of a fix the other day.
I won't forget what you did for me.
npc.recall.knock_night: Knocking at my door in the middle of the night, {name}? Really?
I didn't sleep a wink after you knocked.
npc.recall.project: The village looks better since we finished that work together.
We did a fine job, didn't we, {name}?
Thanks to you, the village keeps growing.

controls.horse: The gallop tires the horse: its bar sits with yours while you ride, and when it is winded it only trots until it gets its breath back. It has weight: it speeds up and stops little by little, the faster it goes the wider it turns, and it slows down for slopes, mud, water and walls. Space jumps a fence with a run-up; without it, it stops. Settings › Game › Riding: Arcade makes it turn and stop more sharply. E with nothing aimed gets off. Brush it, feed it and pat it every day (E on it): a closer bond means a longer gallop, fewer scares and new tricks

nature.note.ciervo: Its antlers fall in late winter and grow back by summer.
nature.note.jabali: It roots up the forest floor with its snout, looking for acorns.
nature.note.cisne: It pairs for life and guards its stretch of lake fiercely.
nature.note.gallina: She talks to her chicks before they even hatch.
nature.note.pato: Its feathers stay dry thanks to an oil it spreads with its beak.
nature.note.vaca: It spends about eight hours a day chewing the cud.
nature.note.oveja: Its wool keeps growing all its life: someone has to shear it.
nature.note.cabra: It climbs where nothing else would and tastes everything on the way.
nature.note.cerdo: Cleaner than its fame: it wallows in mud to cool off.
nature.note.conejo: Its long ears hear danger long before it comes.
nature.note.caballo: It can sleep standing up, but only dreams lying down.
nature.note.perro: It never forgets who gives it treats.
nature.note.gato: It comes when it wants, not when it is called.
nature.note.carpa: It can live for decades in calm, muddy water.
nature.note.perca: It hunts in shoals, chasing small fry near the reeds.
nature.note.trucha: It wants cold, clean water and fights hard on the line.
nature.note.salmon: In autumn it swims up the rivers where it was born.
nature.note.lucio: It waits still among the weeds and strikes like an arrow.
nature.note.anguila: It travels thousands of kilometres to the sea to spawn.
nature.note.sardina: It lives in huge shoals that turn all at once.
nature.note.lubina: It prowls the rocky coast where the waves break.
nature.note.pez_globo: When frightened it swells up like a ball.
nature.note.cangrejo: It walks sideways and pinches whatever comes too close.
nature.note.pez_hielo: Its blood carries its own antifreeze.
nature.note.siluro: The biggest fish in the rivers; it feels for food with its whiskers.
nature.note.pulpo: Eight arms, three hearts and a knack for opening jars.
nature.note.atun: It never stops swimming, not even to sleep.
nature.note.esturion: An ancient fish with bony plates instead of scales.
nature.note.pez_dorado: Every fisher swears they have seen it. Few can prove it.
nature.note.mariposa: It tastes flowers with its feet.
nature.note.mariquita: Its spots warn birds that it tastes bad.
nature.note.saltamontes: It sings by rubbing its legs against its wings.
nature.note.libelula: It hunts on the wing and can even fly backwards.
nature.note.luciernaga: Its light is cold: it glows without burning.
nature.note.escarabajo: Its hard wings are a shield; the soft ones fold underneath.
nature.note.grillo: The warmer the night, the faster it chirps.
nature.note.polilla: It steers by the moon, which is why lamps confuse it.
nature.note.oak: An oak can live for centuries; its acorns feed half the forest.
nature.note.fruit: It blossoms in spring and gives apples by autumn.
nature.note.pine: It keeps its needles all year and smells of resin.
nature.note.snowPine: Its branches slope down so the snow slides off.
nature.note.swampTree: Its roots love wet ground and hold the banks together.
nature.note.palm: It bends with the wind instead of breaking.
nature.note.cactus: It stores water in its stem for months without rain.
nature.note.bush: Birds nest in it, safe behind its thorns.
nature.note.deadBush: It looks dead, but its roots wait for the next rain.
nature.note.margarita: It closes at night and opens again with the sun.
nature.note.diente_leon: Blow on its seed head and the wind sows it far away.
nature.note.nabo: Quick to grow and hardy in the cold.
nature.note.fresa: It wears its seeds on the outside.
nature.note.zanahoria: The root goes deep; the leaves barely give it away.
nature.note.tomate: It needs sun and something to climb.
nature.note.maiz: Each strand of silk becomes one kernel.
nature.note.trigo: Its grain, ground fine, makes the flour for bread.
nature.note.calabaza: It sprawls across the field and never forgives a frost.
